text: Tychon AI demonstrates that the primary failure mode of classical PID-based frequency lock loops --- heading-dependent line-pulling from overlapping NV hyperfine structure --- is correctable by a bounded INT8 FCNN operating as an asymmetry de-embedder on a radiation-tolerant FPGA.

At mission-relevant timescales, the AI-augmented loop reduces Allan deviation at the half-orbit period (τ = 2,700 s) by 96.1% (25.9× deviation reduction), from 16.66 µT to 0.64 µT --- demonstrating that the CNN flattens the long-duration drift curve that renders classical PID unusable for orbital navigation.

The complete hybrid control loop --- SmartHLS PID (II=1, \~48 ns latency, 3,000× margin over 150 µs budget) plus VectorBlox-accelerated INT8 CNN (12.5 KB .vnnx) --- synthesizes on the MPFS250T PolarFire SoC at 25.90% LUT utilization with all clock domains passing post-place-and-route timing closure (worst slack +0.728 ns on the 125 MHz PLL OUT0 domain, with the critical path internal to the integrated PID compute datapath) at \~5.2 W FPGA + MSS subsystem power.

The system is bounded by a hardware-enforced Simplex RTA safety architecture that guarantees absolute stability via the Circle Criterion under sector saturation clamps (Decision-2-Option-C hardcoded outer + AXI-tightenable inner) and slew-rate limiting; an inference-deadline watchdog with bumpless transfer is fully synthesized and instantiated in fabric, with the watchdog timer driving ai_watchdog_timeout from a 200,000-cycle counter at 200 MHz.

Three hardware-enforced boundaries in the FPGA fabric guarantee BIBO stability: sector saturation clamps (±4.5% actuator range, ±2.25 µT for a 50 µT operating field), slew-rate limiting on the AI output derivative, and an inference-deadline watchdog (200,000-cycle counter at 200 MHz, 1.0 ms timeout) that drives deterministic bumpless transfer (rising-edge detector, integral state back-calculation I_new = I_old + u_AI_old, 5.0 µs cooldown).

Nitrogen-Vacancy (NV) diamond magnetometers offer a promising pathway for GPS-independent navigation, with demonstrated room-temperature sensitivities reaching 18 pT/√Hz (Stürner et al., 2021) and 9.4 pT/√Hz without cryogenic assistance (Clevenson et al., 2015).

A µs-class classical PID loop stabilizes the NV ensemble at high bandwidth (\<150 µs), while an INT8-quantized CNN (accelerated by VectorBlox on the RT PolarFire SoC) provides \<1 ms adaptive bias cancellation for heading-dependent and thermally-induced errors that the PID cannot resolve.
The bounded hybrid architecture ensures the AI can never destabilize the sensor --- only improve it.

The foundational stabilization is governed by a strictly proper, deterministic classical PID controller (SmartHLS C++, \~48 ns latency at 125 MHz), ensuring mathematically verifiable, high-bandwidth linear tracking.

The outer stage is a hardcoded OUTER_SECTOR_CLAMP_FRACTION = 0.045 (hls/include/rta_config.hpp:19), synthesized as an immediate constant and untouchable by AXI or SEU; for the nominal out_max=5V, out_min=0V actuator range this gives a ±0.225 V outer bound.

**Slew-Rate Limiting (Temporal Limit).** The discrete derivative du_AI/dt is clamped in hardware to MAX_SLEW_PER_CYCLE = 0.001 (Q16.16, hls/include/rta_config.hpp:24); at 200 MHz fabric clock this corresponds to 200 V/ms maximum actuator command rate.
A third boundary --- an inference-deadline watchdog that triggers deterministic bumpless transfer at the 1.0 ms timeout --- is **fully instantiated** in the Phase I integrated overlay.

The watchdog driver is a standalone hand-coded Verilog module (hdl/watchdog_timer.v, 200 MHz × 200,000-cycle counter with \$clog2-derived width) instantiated in the SmartDesign top as watchdog_timer_0.
The placed netlist confirms the instance survives synthesis: watchdog_timer_0/Primitives consumes 26 LUTs and 20 DFFs per MPFS_ICICLE_KIT_BASE_DESIGN_compile_netlist_hier_resources.csv.

The trigger logic inside nv_pid_top_0 (rising-edge detector on ai_watchdog_timeout, cooldown counter at WATCHDOG_COOLDOWN_CYCLES = 1000 = 5.0 µs at 200 MHz) is also present in the placed netlist alongside the integrator, multipliers, clamps, and slew-limit registers.
Six sub-tests pass: A and B above, plus AXI-widen-rejected, AXI-tighten-accepted, SEU-on-inner-state-outer-holds, and 1 kHz watchdog-chatter cooldown (zero spurious large-step events).
At these field strengths, the directional Zeeman splitting (\~1.4 MHz) falls below the ensemble linewidth (\~2 MHz), collapsing the 8 NV resonance dips into one or two unresolved features.

This physics-driven insight led to the reformulation where the CNN acts as a bounded residual corrector for the PID's heading-dependent line-pulling error, achieving 54.3% reduction in scalar tracking error on held-out validation data and 96.1% reduction in Allan deviation at the half-orbit averaging time (25.9× deviation reduction at τ=2,700 s, direct OADEV).
By predicting a ±2.25 µT residual instead of absolute 0--100 µT, the INT8 quantization achieves \~19 nT/bit effective resolution --- a 20× improvement in dynamic range utilization.

The integrated PID datapath adds approximately +20.5 mW over the prior r3_s22 paper-shell total (2,692.9 mW vs 2,672.4 mW), reflecting the actual switching activity of the 25 DSP multipliers plus integrator and clamp registers now present in the placed netlist.
The DSP power line specifically increases (158.8 → 168.7 mW, +9.9 mW) --- directly attributable to the PID\'s MACC blocks.
The Vectorblox inference engine accounts for the largest single contribution to fabric power at \~610 mW across its clock domains, approximately 23% of total fabric.

The integrated PID contributes \~70--80 mW (composed of integrator, multiplier, AXI slave, and watchdog activity), an order of magnitude above the prior 53.9 mW estimate from the paper-shell where the multipliers were folded.
PCIe SerDes consumes 319.8 mW (11.9%) but is not used in the Tychon design and would be disabled in production.

The 5.2 W figure is the FPGA fabric + MSS subsystem only; the full PNT payload also includes laser excitation (\~2 W), MW drive (\~1 W), ADC (\~0.4 W), photodiode + TIA (\~0.2 W), and design margin, for an estimated 9--10 W total payload power pending Phase II component selection.

The reference design includes components not in the Tychon payload (PCIe at 319.8 mW, unused peripherals) and uses VBX V1000 where Tychon targets V250; a Tychon-specific configuration with V250 and PCIe disabled yields a 3.5--4.0 W FPGA+MSS estimate, leaving ample headroom under the 12 W budget.

The worst slack across the design is **+0.728 ns** on the FIC_0 PLL OUT0 (125 MHz / 8 ns) domain, on a path **internal to the integrated PID compute datapath** (nv_pid_top_0/\.../nv_pid_top_pid_integral_inferred_reg\[2\]:CLK → nv_pid_top_pid_integral_inferred_reg\[24\]:D, delay 6.989 ns under slow_lv_ht conditions).

Three earlier closures (April 2 baseline +0.165 ns, April 28 overlay timed at the integration shell, April 29 r3_s22 +1.215 ns) all closed on a SmartDesign top in which nv_pid_top_0 was pruned by Synplify CL168 and constant-folded by upstream input propagation; their numbers describe an integration shell, not a synthesized PID, and are not directly comparable to r6_s25.

The integrated overlay\'s resource and power growth (+3,128 LUTs, +1.19 pp 4LUT, +20.5 mW fabric, +9.9 mW DSP) versus the prior paper-shell numbers is consistent with real datapath being routed: 25 pipelined gain-multiplier MACC blocks plus integrator and clamp registers add real switching activity.

Slack tightened from +1.215 ns (paper-shell) to +0.728 ns (integrated) --- a 487 ps reduction --- because the multipliers, integrator, and bumpless trigger logic now compete for routing resources alongside the Vectorblox datapath.

Octave-spaced grids straddle this dip without landing on it; linear-in-log interpolation between τ = 2,048 s and τ = 4,096 s averages right through it.

Both paths preserve the formal safety chain composition derived in Section 8.5 (the outer hardcoded clamp guarantees absolute authority bound regardless of inner-clamp configuration; the ISS bound scales linearly with clamp authority).
This advances TRL 4 (Phase I) to TRL 6 (Phase II) and produces operational measurements of the \<1 ms AI inference and \<150 µs PID classical latency budgets.
Three Phase I markers carry a deferred status (Section 8.6 KPP scorecard): on-board AI inference latency, on-board PID classical latency, and total payload power.

Phase I produced the Libero post-P&R timing closure, the VectorBlox simulator inference pass, and the 5.2 W FPGA + MSS subsystem power that constitute the analytical foundation for those measurements.

Because the commercial PolarFire and the space-grade RT PolarFire share an architecturally identical underlying logic fabric, routing matrix, and VectorBlox IP core, the synthesis results achieved in Phase I --- specifically the \~48 ns PID latency, +0.728 ns worst slack on the 125 MHz PLL OUT0 domain (with the critical path internal to the integrated PID compute datapath), and 25.90% resource utilization --- are deterministically representative of the flight hardware logic fabric.
